title: Budgets and refusals
subtitle: Spend, memory and admission are first-class controls, and the system says no with a number instead of degrading
lede: Every resource an agent or a kernel can consume has a stated limit in my systems, and crossing it produces a typed refusal with a reason attached. Dollars per day, device pages per context, key-value memory per request, concurrent sequences per engine, tokens per step. The alternative, letting the system find its own limit by thrashing, stalling or running out of memory mid-step, hides the failure where it is most expensive to find. The limit is explicit and set by a human: a whole number of gibibytes, a dollar figure, a count. Admission checks the limit before load is taken on.
quote: Fail closed where the silent alternative is money, loss or a false result; degrade gracefully where the alternative is merely lower quality.
evidence: Admission control and rate limiting: typed refusals at the door carrying how much was needed, how much was available and whether a retry can help, instead of failing mid-step.
Cloud GPU provisioning with cost controls: a fail-closed daily dollar budget, set by a person on a path agents cannot reach, gating GPU provisioning on local, LAN and cloud hardware.
GPU memory management: an explicit device page pool with per-context floors, targets and bursts, and cache pages reserved for a whole answer at admission.
author: Corey James
